dispatch: lake county criterion G FAR backfill

after.note: far sub-metric fully resolved (94.1 -> 100.0). Overall G metric now bound by density (94.6), which is out of scope for this dispatch.

method: For each zoning_district with max_far NULL and far_regulated NULL/unset that had auction-linked parcels (128 lake auction parcels joined against v_zoning_gold_standard_card), researched the primary ordinance/code to determine whether FAR genuinely applies. In every case investigated, the jurisdiction's code regulates residential development via density (DU/acre), lot coverage, and/or impervious surface ratio -- NOT floor area ratio. Rather than inventing FAR numbers, set zoning_districts.far_regulated=false so v_zoning_district_applicability.far_applicable correctly excludes these districts from the FAR denominator.

districts_updated.evidence: Sec.25-280 Table 4-3 (nonresidential districts incl. C-1): columns are Density(DU/A), Lot Area/Width, Setbacks, Height, ISR, Open Space -- no FAR column exists anywhere in Leesburg's Chapter 25 zoning code.
Sec.25-280 Table 4-2 (residential districts incl. R-2): same column set as Table 4-3, no FAR.

districts_updated.jurisdiction_name: Leesburg (row description indicates this is actually unincorporated Lake County's R-4 district, mis-tagged jurisdiction_id -- flagged, not corrected, out of scope for this FAR fix)
districts_updated.evidence: Unincorporated Lake County LDR Sec 3.02.03.A: 'For purposes of these regulations, Floor area ratios (FAR) are provided only for non-residential Development.' Table 3.02.06 Note 2 restates: 'FAR: Floor Area Ratio. FAR applies only to non-residential Development.' R-4 is a residential district (Medium Suburban Residential).
LDC Sec.3.4.2 Site development standards table for R-1AAAA/R-1AAA/R-1AA/R-1A/R-1/R-1B: rows are lot size, lot width, street frontage, setbacks, height, dwelling size, parking -- no FAR row.

LDC Sec.3.4.3 Site development standards table for R-2 Duplex district: same structure as R-1 tables, no FAR row. Mount Dora only applies FAR to commercial/mixed-use districts (C-1=0.25, C-2 varies, WBI-E etc.).

LDC Ch.5 RS-6 design standards: lot area, lot width, setbacks, 'maximum impervious surface ratio' (45%), minimum floor area (1,000 sf), max height -- same non-FAR pattern used by RS-4 and other residential districts in the same chapter.

Code Sec.125-167 'Lot and height requirements' for R-1: lot size, lot width, impervious surface coverage (55% max), height -- no FAR section exists anywhere in Division 5 (Intent/Permitted Uses/Conditional Uses/Lot&Height/Yards).

districts_updated.note: no prior zone_standards row existed -- INSERTed new row with source_url/confidence_score/ordinance_section only (no dimensional numbers, since far_regulated=false)
districts_updated.evidence: Table 8-3 Development Standards covers all current Tavares districts (RSF-E/A/1/2, RMF-2/3, RMH-S/P, MU, C-1/C-2, CD, I, PFD, PD) using Maximum Impervious Surface Area exclusively; 'Floor Area Ratio' does not appear anywhere in Ch.8. 'R-6' is not a current Tavares district code (legacy/renamed), so this is inferred by code-wide pattern rather than a direct R-6-labeled table row.
Table 8-3 RMF-2 row: Maximum Impervious Surface Area (60%/70% townhomes) -- no FAR row.

districts_updated.evidence: Table 8-3 RMF-3 row: Maximum Impervious Surface Area (70%) -- no FAR row.
Table 8-3 RMH-S row: Maximum Impervious Surface Area (50%) -- no FAR row.
Table 8-3 RSF-1 row: Maximum Impervious Surface Area (60%) -- no FAR row.
Table 8-3 RSF-2 row: Maximum Impervious Surface Area (60%) -- no FAR row.

districts_updated.note: no prior zone_standards row existed -- INSERTed new row with source_url/confidence_score/ordinance_section only
districts_updated.source_url: https://eustis.civicweb.net/document/34258/Exhibits%20A%20thru%20I%20with%20Proposed%20Revisions.pdf (Comprehensive Plan 2035, FLUE Table A-3.1 Future Land Use Designations)
districts_updated.evidence: Eustis Comp Plan Sec FLU A-2: 'The City of Eustis does not have zoning districts.' Table A-3.1 shows Intensity Range (FAR) = N/A for every residential FLU designation (SR, UR, MH). 'RT' (Rural Transition, per existing DB description used as zoning proxy) is not itself a named FLUE category in Table A-3.1, so this is inferred by analogy to the other residential FLU categories rather than a direct table match -- flagged INFERRED with lower confidence.
FLUE Table A-3.1: 'Suburban Residential (SR)' row -- Maximum Net Density = 5 dwelling units/acre (exact match to existing DB max_density_du_acre=5.0), Intensity Range (Floor Area Ratio) = 'N/A'.

R-18 (legacy code) renamed to R-3 'Low Density Residential District' per Ch.6 zoning regs renaming table. R-3 section states 'gross density shall not exceed three (3) units per acre' (matches existing DB density=3.0). No FAR mentioned in R-3's permitted-uses section; only the separate CBD dimensional chart (a different district) uses ISR, not FAR, and does not apply to R-3. Marked INFERRED because the R-3 section itself never explicitly denies FAR (absence of mention, not an explicit N/A statement like Leesburg/Mount Dora/Tavares/Eustis).

LDR dimensional table: LD-SFR row has no FAR value (column blank); FAR only appears for Commercial (PO=0.50 max) and Industrial (LM/HI=0.75 max) rows. LD-SFR density 1-4 units/acre matches existing DB (4.0); parking 'Capacity for two automobiles' matches existing DB parking_per_unit=2.0.

LDR dimensional table: MD-SFR row has no FAR value; FAR only for Commercial/Industrial rows. Density 4-8 units/acre matches existing DB (8.0); parking 'Capacity for one automobile' matches existing DB parking_per_unit=1.0.

residual_unresolved.reason_not_fixed: Groveland's Community Development Code Art.5 Sec.5.2 (ART5ZO) loads its dimensional tables via client-side JS that neither WebFetch nor r.jina.ai could render (returned nav-shell only). Secondary sources (Groveland FLUE Chapter 1 PDF, web search) gave inconsistent/unverifiable density figures (4.0 vs existing DB's 6.0) and no FAR confirmation either way. Left untouched rather than guess -- BLANK > WRONG per honesty protocol.
residual_unresolved.status: UNKNOWN -- requires follow-up session with working access to Groveland CDC Art.5 Sec.5.2 or a Firecrawl/browser-based fetch of the JS-rendered page
